BLOCKED: (a) 2-user typing-indicator + read-receipt cross-user WS test could NOT be executed — same WS endpoint failure as iter 382/383: 'WebSocket is closed before the connection is established' on wss://video-meet-pro.preview.emergentagent.com/api/ws/chat/user_<id> (5 attempts per chat-page load). The iter 383 .send()/.readyState code is unchanged, correct by inspection, but at runtime ws.readyState never reaches OPEN so no typing/read frames are emitted. (b) PREVIEW-ENV ISSUE (NOT introduced by iter 384, but newly observed): the 'Made with Emergent' badge (a#emergent-badge fixed bottom-right) INTERCEPTS pointer events on data-testid='chat-send-btn' at 1920x1080 viewport — Playwright reports 'subtree intercepts pointer events' and no POST fires. Using Enter key to send (which the input's onKeyDown handler supports) works perfectly. Real users on smaller viewports or in production (no badge) are unaffected. Code review of all 4 new components confirms behaviour-preserving extraction: MessageInput onClick={sendMessage}+onKeyDown Enter wiring is correct, MessageBubble props/render unchanged from iter 383, MessageList forwardRef correctly forwards messagesEndRef for scroll-into-view, ChatSidebar exports filter-chips/search/new-chat/sound with all testids intact.

ui_bugs.issue: Send button is fully covered by the 'Made with Emergent' badge anchor (a#emergent-badge, fixed position bottom-right) at 1920x1080 viewport in the preview env. Result: clicking data-testid='chat-send-btn' (even with force=True in some browsers) fails because the anchor intercepts pointer events; the POST never fires and the input is not cleared. The bubble appears only via Enter key. This is a layout collision specific to the preview-env badge, not a regression from the iter 384 refactor, but it makes data-testid='chat-send-btn' un-clickable in the preview env. Workaround in tests: send via input keyboard.press('Enter'). Suggested fix: bump send-btn z-index above the badge (e.g. z-[60]) or add a right-padding margin to the input bar so the button does not occupy the bottom-right 80x40px area where the badge sits.

integration_issues.issue: wss://video-meet-pro.preview.emergentagent.com/api/ws/chat/<user_id> repeatedly fails with 'WebSocket is closed before the connection is established.' (5 attempts seen on every /chat page load). Because the socket never reaches readyState===OPEN, handle.send() always returns false and no typing/read frames are transmitted. This makes the 2-user typing-indicator and read-receipt e2e tests UN-TESTABLE in the preview env. Same issue as iter 382 and iter 383. The iter 383 .send/.readyState code itself is correct by inspection.

action_items: FIX preview-env send-button overlap: bump data-testid='chat-send-btn' z-index above the 'Made with Emergent' badge (the badge sits at fixed bottom-right with high z-index) OR add safe-area padding to the right of MessageInput so the send button is not in the bottom-right corner. This is a real, reproducible UI bug — a normal user click on the send button in preview env fails. The Button already has 'relative z-20' inline; the badge appears to be higher. Try z-[100] on the button or wrap MessageInput bottom in a container with right padding ~96px on screens where the badge is shown.

Without this, typing-indicator and read-receipt cross-user e2e cannot be observed. The newly-reactivated qa_member@meetflow.com / QaMember2026! credential is ready to use once the WS endpoint is fixed.

OPTIONAL — add a small unit test for createChatWebSocket that mocks the global WebSocket and asserts handle.send() returns true only when readyState===1 and false otherwise. This lets future regressions of the iter 383 fix be caught without depending on the live WS endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: MessageInput.js line 105-112: Send button has `relative z-20`, which is BELOW the Emergent preview badge. Either bump to z-[60] or, better, mount the badge-collision-prone region inside a container that has right-padding on preview env. Production users won't see the badge, but the test pipeline does, and humans on small viewports will also see partial overlap.

ChatPage.js is now 989 lines — refactor goal of <700 lines not yet met. The remaining bulk is conversation-fetch + WebSocket setup + new-chat dialog + add-member dialog (~250 lines) which can each be extracted into a custom hook (useChatWebSocket, useConversations) and a NewChatDialog component. Aim for ChatPage to be <500 lines of orchestrator code.

MessageInput.js receives 16 props — consider grouping (gifOpen/setGifOpen/gifQuery/gifResults/searchGifs/sendGif) into a single `gif` object prop and (recording/startRecording/stopRecording) into a single `voice` object prop. Same readability concern as raised for MessageBubble in iter 383.

ChatSidebar.js ChatSoundToggle (line 26-93): the volume-btn is conditionally rendered with `!muted && (...)` — if the testid 'chat-sound-volume-btn' is expected to be always present by the test suite (per the test instructions in this iteration), this should be made explicit in the doc / test playbook. Otherwise a test that clicks chat-sound-toggle first (toggling to muted) will lose access to the volume-btn DOM node.

sendMessage in ChatPage.js still uses catch { toast.error('Nachricht konnte nicht gesendet werden') } and swallows the server detail — surface err?.response?.data?.detail like deleteConversation() so production failures stay diagnosable.

rca of the issue: Two distinct issues observed: (A) chat-send-btn click failure in preview env = pure layout collision between the bottom-right 'Made with Emergent' badge anchor (added by the preview platform) and the Send Button. The button has `relative z-20`, but the badge is higher in the stacking context. Fix: bump send-btn z-index above the badge OR move it inboard with safe-area padding. (B) typing/read-receipt 2-user push silently no-op = WS endpoint never reaches OPEN. Iter 383's .send/.readyState code (chatWebSocket.js lines 136-148) is correct: when readyState!==1 it returns false. Today the readyState is always 0/3 because the socket is closed before connect. Fix order: first fix the WS endpoint (ingress + handler), then re-run the 2-user e2e.
